answer: SESSION_COOKIE_PATH defaults to "/" (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py). It is used in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py (SessionMiddleware.process_response): as path= in response.delete_cookie (line 39) and in response.set_cookie (line 72).

EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD is defined in django/conf/global_settings.py with a default of "" (an empty string). It is used in django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py, where EmailBackend.__init__ sets self.password = settings.EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD if no password argument is passed. The send_mail and send_mass_mail docstrings in django/core/mail/__init__.py also mention it.

SECURE_SSL_HOST is read in `corpus/django/middleware/security.py` (line 15), where `SecurityMiddleware` assigns it to `self.redirect_host`. Its default is `None`, set in `corpus/django/conf/global_settings.py`.

DATABASE_ROUTERS is read in django/db/utils.py by ConnectionRouter.routers (a cached_property), which falls back to settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS when no routers are passed to ConnectionRouter. It is also referenced in makemigrations.py (consistency check) and test/signals.py (cache clearing). Its default value is an empty list, [], defined in django/conf/global_settings.py.

`LANGUAGE_COOKIE_DOMAIN` is defined in `conf/global_settings.py` with a default of `None`. It is used in `views/i18n.py` (around line 63), where it is passed as the `domain` argument to `response.set_cookie(...)` when the language is set.

`CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` defaults to `False` (in `conf/global_settings.py`). It is read in `middleware/csrf.py` when setting the CSRF cookie, and in `core/checks/security/csrf.py`, where the `security.W016` deploy check warns if it isn't `True`.

DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS is used in CommonMiddleware.process_request (django/middleware/common.py), which loops over settings.DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS and raises PermissionDenied("Forbidden user agent") if a regex matches the request's User-Agent. Its default, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py, is an empty list: []

STATICFILES_DIRS defaults to an empty list ([]), defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is used mainly by FileSystemFinder in django/contrib/staticfiles/finders.py, which reads settings.STATICFILES_DIRS to locate static files and to run system checks. It is also read in core/checks/caches.py and test/signals.py.

SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY defaults to `True` in `django/conf/global_settings.py`. It is read in `django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py` (when setting the session cookie), `django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py` (when setting the messages cookie), and `django/core/checks/security/sessions.py` (the security checks W013–W015).

The default is True, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is read in django/conf/urls/i18n.py (i18n_patterns returns the URLs unchanged if it is False), django/utils/cache.py (lines 339 and 419), django/utils/translation/__init__.py (line 65, which chooses trans_real or trans_null) and django/utils/translation/reloader.py (line 13).

The default of STATIC_ROOT is None, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is used mainly in contrib/staticfiles: storage.py (StaticFilesStorage location = settings.STATIC_ROOT), finders.py (check that STATICFILES_DIRS doesn't contain it), utils.py (must differ from MEDIA_ROOT), collectstatic command, plus core/checks/caches.py, makemessages.py, test/signals.py and test/testcases.py.

EMAIL_USE_SSL is read in `django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py` (line 34), where `self.use_ssl` falls back to it when no `use_ssl` argument is passed. Its default is `False`, set in `django/conf/global_settings.py`.

CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW is used in django/middleware/csrf.py by _get_failure_view(), which returns get_callable(settings.CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW). The system check check_csrf_failure_view in django/core/checks/security/csrf.py also uses it. Its default is "django.views.csrf.csrf_failure", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py.

The default is "django.contrib.sessions.backends.db", defined in global_settings.py. The setting is used via import_module(settings.SESSION_ENGINE) in contrib/sessions/middleware.py (SessionMiddleware), the clearsessions command, and test/client.py (session property, login, logout).

`FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS` is read in `django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py` (in `directory_permissions_mode`, around line 61) and `django/core/files/storage/memory.py` (around line 205). Its default in `conf/global_settings.py` is `None`.

`SESSION_COOKIE_AGE` is defined in `corpus/django/conf/global_settings.py` (around line 476) with a default of `60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 2`, which is 1,209,600 seconds (two weeks). It is read in `corpus/django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py` (line 197) by `get_session_cookie_age()`, which returns `settings.SESSION_COOKIE_AGE`.
The setting is read in `django/views/i18n.py` (in `set_language`), where it is passed as `httponly=` to `response.set_cookie(...)`. Its default is `False`, set in `django/conf/global_settings.py`.

`IGNORABLE_404_URLS` is read in `corpus/django/middleware/common.py` at line 178, where it checks whether a URI matches any pattern. Its default is an empty list (`[]`), set in `corpus/django/conf/global_settings.py` at line 257.

SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE defaults to `"Lax"` in `corpus/django/conf/global_settings.py` (line 484). It is used in `corpus/django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py` (around lines 38 and 75) and in `corpus/django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py` (around line 119).

LOGGING_CONFIG is used in django/__init__.py (setup()), which calls configure_logging(settings.LOGGING_CONFIG, settings.LOGGING). configure_logging in django/utils/log.py imports the callable via import_string and invokes it with the LOGGING settings. Default value: "logging.config.dictConfig" (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py).

LOGIN_URL defaults to "/accounts/login/" (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py). It is used as a fallback in django/contrib/auth/mixins.py (AccessMixin.get_login_url), and in django/contrib/auth/views.py (logout_then_login and redirect_to_login).

SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT defaults to `False` (`conf/global_settings.py`). It is read in `middleware/security.py` (line 15, `self.redirect = settings.SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`) and in the deploy check `check_ssl_redirect` in `core/checks/security/base.py` (line 201).

CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS defaults to "default". It is defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is read in django/middleware/cache.py, where UpdateCacheMiddleware.__init__ (around line 73) and FetchFromCacheMiddleware.__init__ (around line 142) set self.cache_alias = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS. CacheMiddleware falls back to DEFAULT_CACHE_ALIAS when cache_alias is None.

The default TIME_ZONE is "America/Chicago", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is used in several places. conf/__init__.py (around line 214) validates it and sets os.environ["TZ"] and calls time.tzset(). utils/timezone.py uses it as the default time zone. test/signals.py resets the process time zone when the setting changes. The postgresql backend also sets the connection time zone.

SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN defaults to `None`, meaning a standard domain cookie. It is read in `django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py` (when setting and deleting the session cookie), `django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py` (when deleting the messages cookie), and `django/test/client.py` (when setting login cookies).

MIGRATION_MODULES defaults to `{}` in `django/conf/global_settings.py`. It is read mainly in `MigrationLoader.migrations_module()` in `django/db/migrations/loader.py`, and also in `django/db/migrations/writer.py` and `django/db/backends/base/creation.py`.

STATIC_URL defaults to `None` (defined in `conf/global_settings.py`). It is read in `templatetags/static.py` (`do_static` joins paths with it), in `contrib/staticfiles/utils.py` (`check_settings` raises `ImproperlyConfigured` if it is unset), and in `test/signals.py` (changing it resets the storages).

SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS defaults to 0 (HSTS disabled), defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is read in SecurityMiddleware.__init__ (django/middleware/security.py:11, `self.sts_seconds = settings.SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS`). It is also used in the deploy system checks in django/core/checks/security/base.py: W004 warns when it is unset, and check_sts_include_subdomains and check_sts_preload skip their checks when it is 0.

The setting is read in SecurityMiddleware.__init__ (django/middleware/security.py:19, self.cross_origin_opener_policy = settings.SECURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_OPENER_POLICY) and applied in process_response to set the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header (security.py:61). It is also validated by the check_cross_origin_opener_policy system check (django/core/checks/security/base.py:274, error E024). Its default is "same-origin", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:658.

The default is False, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. The setting is read in django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py, in get_expire_at_browser_close(), which returns settings.SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE when the session has no custom expiry. The session middleware (django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) calls that method when it sets the session cookie.

The session middleware in `contrib/sessions/middleware.py` reads `SESSION_COOKIE_PATH` when it sets or deletes the session cookie. If a project doesn't set it, the value is `"/"`, from `conf/global_settings.py`.

The SMTP email backend, `EmailBackend.__init__` in `django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py`, reads `settings.EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD` when no explicit password is passed. If the project doesn't set it, the value is the empty string `""` from `django/conf/global_settings.py`.

The security middleware (`corpus/django/middleware/security.py`, line 15) reads `settings.SECURE_SSL_HOST` into `self.redirect_host`. If a project does not set it, the value is `None`, per `global_settings.py`.

The `routers` cached property on `ConnectionRouter` in `django/db/utils.py` reads `settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS`. When a project doesn't set it, the value is the empty list `[]` from `global_settings.py`.
The `set_language` view in `django/views/i18n.py` passes `settings.LANGUAGE_COOKIE_DOMAIN` to `response.set_cookie(...)`. When a project doesn't set it, the default in `global_settings.py` is `None`.

CsrfViewMiddleware (django/middleware/csrf.py, in _set_csrf_cookie) reads settings.CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE and passes it as secure= to response.set_cookie. The default in django/conf/global_settings.py is False. The security check W016 also reads it.

The `CommonMiddleware` in `django/middleware/common.py` reads `settings.DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS` and raises `PermissionDenied` on a match. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `global_settings.py` is an empty list (`[]`), so no user agents are blocked.

The `FileSystemFinder` class in `django/contrib/staticfiles/finders.py` reads `STATICFILES_DIRS` to locate static files. If a project doesn't set it, the default in `global_settings.py` is an empty list (`[]`).

The session middleware (SessionMiddleware in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) reads SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY when it sets the session cookie, passing httponly=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY or None. The messages cookie storage and the security system checks (W013/W015) also read it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is True.

USE_I18N defaults to `True` when a project doesn't set it, per `conf/global_settings.py`. The snippet only shows a comment in `utils/translation/__init__.py` that refers to `settings.USE_I18N`, so that module is the likely reader, but the actual read isn't in the code shown.

Django's staticfiles app reads `STATIC_ROOT`, including the storage backend (its default `location`), the system checks in `contrib/staticfiles/finders.py` and `utils.py`, and the test case `get_base_dir`. If a project doesn't set it, the default in `conf/global_settings.py` is `None`.

The SMTP email backend's `__init__` in `django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py` reads `settings.EMAIL_USE_SSL` when no `use_ssl` argument is passed. If the project doesn't set it, the value is `False`, as defined in `conf/global_settings.py`.

The `_get_failure_view()` function in `django/middleware/csrf.py` reads `settings.CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW`, and if a project doesn't set it, the default is `"django.views.csrf.csrf_failure"` from `global_settings.py`.

The Django test client (`django/test/client.py`) reads `SESSION_ENGINE` via `import_module(settings.SESSION_ENGINE)`. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `global_settings.py` is `"django.contrib.sessions.backends.db"`.

The storage classes read it: FileSystemStorage.directory_permissions_mode (core/files/storage/filesystem.py:61; InMemoryStorage does the same in memory.py:205) uses it via _value_or_setting when no explicit directory_permissions_mode is passed. If a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings.py is None, so no explicit mode is applied to created directories (the OS umask default applies).

`SESSION_COOKIE_AGE` is read by `get_session_cookie_age()` in `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py`, which is used by the session backends when computing expiry and by the signed-cookies backend. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `global_settings.py` is `60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 2`, which is 1,209,600 seconds (two weeks).

The `set_language` view in `django/views/i18n.py` reads `LANGUAGE_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` when it sets the language cookie. If a project does not set it, the value is `False`, per `django/conf/global_settings.py`.
The `is_ignorable_request` method in `django/middleware/common.py` reads `settings.IGNORABLE_404_URLS`, and it defaults to an empty list (`[]`) in `conf/global_settings.py`.

The session middleware (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py`) reads `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE` when setting or deleting the session cookie, and the messages cookie storage also reads it. If a project doesn't set it, Django's `global_settings.py` default is `"Lax"`.

`django/__init__.py` reads `settings.LOGGING_CONFIG` and passes it to `configure_logging` in `utils/log.py`. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `conf/global_settings.py` is `"logging.config.dictConfig"`.

The `AccessMixin.get_login_url()` method in `django/contrib/auth/mixins.py` reads `settings.LOGIN_URL` as a fallback, and it defaults to `"/accounts/login/"` from `conf/global_settings.py` when a project doesn't set it. `redirect_to_login()` and `logout_then_login()` in `contrib/auth/views.py` also read it.

The `SecurityMiddleware` in `django/middleware/security.py` reads `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` into `self.redirect`, and the `check_ssl_redirect` system check also reads it. When a project doesn't set it, the default from `django/conf/global_settings.py` is `False`.

The cache middleware in `django/middleware/cache.py` reads it: `UpdateCacheMiddleware` and `FetchFromCacheMiddleware` both set `self.cache_alias = settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS` in `__init__`. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `global_settings.py` is `"default"`.

`django/utils/timezone.py` reads `settings.TIME_ZONE` and returns it as a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`. When a project doesn't set it, Django uses the default from `global_settings.py`, which is `"America/Chicago"`.

The session middleware (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py`) reads `SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN` when setting or deleting the session cookie. If a project doesn't set it, the default in `global_settings.py` is `None`, which means a standard host-only domain cookie.

The migration loader reads it: `MigrationLoader.migrations_module()` in django/db/migrations/loader.py checks whether the app label is in settings.MIGRATION_MODULES. The test database creation code in django/db/backends/base/creation.py also reads and temporarily overrides it. If a project doesn't set it, it takes the default from django/conf/global_settings.py, which is an empty dict `{}`.

Several parts read `STATIC_URL`, including `check_settings` in `contrib/staticfiles/utils.py`, the `static` context processor, and `contrib/staticfiles/storage.py`. When a project doesn't set it, the default in `conf/global_settings.py` is `None`, and `check_settings` then raises `ImproperlyConfigured`.

`SecurityMiddleware.__init__` in `django/middleware/security.py` reads `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS` into `self.sts_seconds`. If a project doesn't set it, Django uses the default of `0` from `conf/global_settings.py`, which disables HSTS.

The `SecurityMiddleware` class in `middleware/security.py` reads it in `__init__` and sets the `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` header on responses. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `conf/global_settings.py` is `"same-origin"`.

The `get_expire_at_browser_close()` method in `corpus/django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py` reads it as a fallback when no session expiry is stored. When a project doesn't set it, the value is `False`, per `conf/global_settings.py`.
